subject: Coordination: API v1/model deprecation & migration plan (timeline + exceptions)
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Coordination: API v1/model deprecation & migration plan (timeline + exceptions)

Team —

We need to lock the cross-functional plan for deprecating the v1/generate API and the legacy model family (redwood-legacy-1) and migrating customers to the v2/responses + redwood-advanced-2 family. Engineering has indicated this is blocking some infra changes, and Sales/CS will need clear comms and an exceptions process.

High-level ask: please review the attached timeline and migration playbook and weight in on the operational asks and exception flows by Monday EOD.

Key constraints to consider:
- Target deprecation window: start of Q4 (tentatively 2026-10-01) for turn-down of v1 for new requests; final shutoff 2026-12-15.
- We must provide automatic compatibility shim for the most common SDK patterns, but some enterprise customers will need manual migration and test windows.
- Legal/contract exceptions must be tracked and limited to documented cases (see Markus).

Immediate items:
1) Dev: confirm whether we can support a 6-week staged rollout for the compatibility shim + opt-in telemetry. Any additional infra requirements?
2) Sales: we need a customer comms template and a list of customers who should get a dedicated migration window (big spenders / slow internal cert).
3) CS: define migration support SLAs and offer packaging for paid migration assistance.
4) Legal: outline the contractual exception criteria and approval flow.

Attachments: deprecation_timeline_v1.xlsx, migration_playbook_v1.2.md

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: API v1/model deprecation & migration plan (timeline + exceptions)

Thanks Laura — quick engineering notes after skimming the playbook:

- Compatibility shim: doable, but we estimate ~4 engineering weeks + 2 weeks of testing to cover our top-10 SDK patterns (Python, Node, Java). We can reduce to 3 weeks if we scope to only Python+Node initially and add feature flags.
- Autoscaling risk: during the migration window we should reserve burst capacity for customer-led replays; recommend a scheduled warm pool for heavy customers rather than full overprovisioning.
- Telemetry: to detect clients still on v1 we need a short-lived sampling flag (non-PII) — safe to enable.

Open questions for Product:
A) Is the proposed 10/01 start for the staged rollout flexible by ±3 weeks? If not, we'll need to compress QA and possibly restrict language bindings in the first phase.
B) For customers that request a long-tail exception, do we have a maximum extension (e.g., 6 months) or only case-by-case? That impacts service-level planning.

I'll drop a short PR with the compatibility shim prototype by Friday.

— Dev
Lead, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: API v1/model deprecation & migration plan (timeline + exceptions)

Laura / team —

Sales input: we need the comms and the migration offer nailed down ASAP. A few notes from the field and Acme (they're cc'd on a separate thread):

- Customers want a clear "what changes for my app" doc. The playbook is great but needs a one-pager. Can Marketing and Product sign off on a one-pager before next Wed (6/24)?
- Exception candidates: Acme Corp (enterprise platform), Meridian Health (HIPAA integrations), and two smaller partners that have strict change windows.
- Pricing: recommend we make basic migration support free for all accounts and charge for dedicated migration engineering (block of hours) for enterprise exceptions. We should standardize a migration SKU.

Action for CS & Product: Vivek, can you produce a prioritized list of customers who need >1 week of hands-on migration? I'll start outreach once we have the one-pager.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Senior Account Executive, Americas
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: API v1/model deprecation & migration plan (timeline + exceptions)

Looping in specifics from CS perspective —

- Prioritized exception list (initial):
  * Acme Corp — large enterprise, running v1 across multiple teams; requests 90-day migration window and access to dedicated migration engineers.
  * Meridian Health — requires on-prem test harness for compliance certification; needs extended window (up to 6 months) and SOC2 evidence for any telemetry changes.
  * Starline Logistics — small but uses custom model adapters; willing to pay for migration services.

- Support SLAs we propose:
  * Standard: self-serve docs + 2-week callback for troubleshooting.
  * Assisted Migration (paid SKU): 20 business hours guaranteed onboarding support within a 30-day window.
  * Enterprise Migration: 90-day dedicated window + weekly migration syncs, reserved engineering time (quoted separately).

- For Acme specifically: they've raised a procurement question about a contractual exception to extend v1 until 2027-03-31. They need this in writing to sign the renewal.

I will compile a full customer list and share a spreadsheet by EOD Monday.

— Vivek
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: API v1/model deprecation & migration plan (timeline + exceptions)

Folks —

A few legal points to bake into the process:

1) Contractual exceptions: any extension beyond the published deprecation timeline must be handled via an amendment and signed PO. No verbal commitments. Sales must not promise date-specific exceptions without Legal loop-in.

2) Compliance/telemetry: Meridian's SOC2 ask is standard — telemetry that includes hashed client identifiers is fine but avoid persistent user identifiers. For on-prem customers, we need to document the telemetry toggles and include an opt-in checkbox in the migration playbook.

3) Escalation: define an approval bucket for exec-signed exceptions (limit to 3 active enterprise exceptions at a time). Approval should include cost recovery for reserved infra.

I will draft a short "Exception Amendment" template (2 pages) and circulate for comment by Tuesday.

-Markus
General Counsel
Redwood Inference
